findings.title: DHW planner prices COP at current humidity, not the forecast; published DHW runs up to 5 K below the plan
findings.claim: With a learned humid-bucket defrost derate and a humidity forecast that differs from the current reading, the DHW schedule the optimizer chooses, re-simulated through ThermalModel.simulate_dhw_only (the model every DHW planning stage runs), deviates from the published OptimizationResult.dhw_temp_trajectory by 3.27 to 4.97 K over six weather x humidity cells, and the planner buys 13-15 % less DHW electricity (4.848 vs 5.624 kWh on winter_mild) than it does when the current humidity equals the forecast.
findings.mechanism: ThermalModel.extend_dhw_temps/simulate_dhw_only call compute_cop_dhw(outdoor, temp) with no humidity, and so do the optimizer's DHW planning seams (optimizer.py compute_cop_dhw / marginal_cop('dhw') calls at 3297, 4315, 4961, 5344, 5358, 5462, 5741); _cop_law then falls back to params.ambient_humidity, which the coordinator sets to the CURRENT reading (coordinator.py:5398). simulate_trajectory_with_dhw passes the per-step forecast humidity. The DefrostDerate factor is humidity-dependent, so the planner and the physics price the same DHW kWh at different COPs.

findings.phenomenon_property: Every COP evaluated for a future horizon step -- planner, settlement, cap refund, baseline -- is evaluated at that step's forecast humidity, the one simulate_trajectory_with_dhw uses; no future-step COP falls back to the current reading while a forecast series exists.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Give extend_dhw_temps/simulate_dhw_only an optional per-step humidity array and pass h.humidity from every optimizer DHW planning seam (and from the other future-step COP calls the seam rule lists); fixtures with no humidity series stay byte-identical.
expected_golden_drift: none expected: no golden scenario passes a humidity series together with a learned derate

findings.title: Two COP laws for one lift: DHW tank priced up to 45 % more efficient than a buffer at the same water temperature
findings.claim: With cop_flow_carnot on, marginal_cop(o,'dhw',T)/marginal_cop(o,'buffer',T) exceeds 1.01 in 102 of 105 grid cells (T 40-70 C, outdoor -15..12 C, three nameplates), max 1.4548 at 70 C / 7 C, and compute_cop_dhw grants a 12 % boost over the space curve below the 35 C reference that the space/buffer law refuses by design.
findings.mechanism: compute_cop_dhw applies a linear, outdoor-independent penalty max(0.5, 1-0.008*(T-35)) that is two-sided about 35 C, while the buffer (and the direct-plant curve) use the Carnot ratio flow_lift_factor, which is one-sided and outdoor-dependent. The same compressor lifting water to the same temperature gets two different COPs depending on which tank the water is in; a coil-fed DHW tank should be at or below, not above, the buffer. The DHW law also overstates the warm-vs-cold advantage at 55 C (1.4286 vs 1.2500), so DHW timing and DHW-vs-buffer charging are valued on inconsistent physics.

evidence.machine: 4-vCPU cloud container, 15 GB, shared with up to 13 seats (not the audit box)

perturbation.change: one-line production edit (harness --perturb, class-attribute swap restored in finally): in compute_cop_dhw replace the linear dhw_penalty with self.flow_lift_factor(outdoor_temp, dhw_temp)

findings.metric_definition: max over 105 (nameplate, tank temp, outdoor) cells of marginal_cop(o,'dhw',T)/marginal_cop(o,'buffer',T) with cop_flow_carnot=True

null_control.note: at the 35 C reference flow both laws agree exactly (RESULT null_at_reference_flow)

findings.phenomenon_property: One lift, one price: the COP at which heat enters any water store at temperature T and outdoor o is a single function of (o, T) up to an explicit, documented coil-approach penalty that can only lower it.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Derive the DHW penalty from flow_lift_factor (plus an optional coil approach delta) behind the cop_flow_carnot flag, so fixtures without the flag stay byte-identical; decide explicitly whether a sub-35 C tank earns a boost in both laws or in neither.
expected_golden_drift: fixtures with cop_flow_carnot and DHW, e.g. everything_on, wood_coil (if the flag is set there)

non_findings.claim: simulate_trajectory_batch is bitwise identical to simulate_trajectory on 600 random cases x 5 rows across 8 input kinds (single, two-zone, valve, Carnot, wood two-tank, direct slab, capped buffer, flow-curve COP) with learned derate, NaN humidity, internal-gains profile, valve targets, external heat and dt 0.25/1 h
dt-invariance: end-state error vs a 1/32 h reference halves with dt (first-order Euler); throttled buffers substep so 1 h, 30 min and 15 min steps integrate identically

Monotonicity over trajectories: +1e-3 kW at any earlier step never lowers any later store temperature (valved Carnot buffer 35-300 L, 3-12 kW, tank start 30/60 C) despite the COP-vs-tank-temperature coupling
Buffer and DHW caps clamp the charging rate, not the state: a tank read 5 K above its cap cools at its physical rate in an idle step instead of snapping to the cap
compute_cop and compute_cop_dhw are monotone non-decreasing in outdoor and non-increasing in flow/tank temperature across 5 configurations on a 551x56 grid

DefrostDerate.factor stays inside [DERATE_MIN, 1] and is continuous across bucket edges and the 0/5 C band edges (max step 4.29e-4 per 0.01 K / 0.01 %RH); note it is non-unity up to 0.18 just outside the learning band because the interpolation support reaches the adjacent centres (-2.5 and 6.5 C), not pursued as a finding

simulate_dhw_step's inlet floor injects heat (booked, conservative) only when a tank is drawn at more than ~3x its volume inside a 1 h window: 45/288 configs at dt 0.25 h, all but a 0.05 kW case in tanks <= 100 L
non_findings.value: dhw_floor_hits=45/288; max 0.0500 kW for tanks >= 150 L
